title: Scheduler/trigger-liveness health and outcome/yield health must remain independently representable
requirement: Where a Clank's health or alerting model depends on distinguishing whether scheduled collection is running from whether it is producing useful results, the Clank MUST keep at least two dimensions independently representable: operational execution/liveness health (is the trigger firing, is the process reaching and successfully exiting) and output/yield health (is the collection actually producing new or expected observations). Success on one dimension MUST NOT be presented, directly or by omission, as success on the other. Where source-level output is meaningful, a source producing zero new observations MUST be classifiable as healthy, anomalous, or unknown according to that source's own expected behavior — zero output MUST NOT be silently collapsed into a single undifferentiated 'healthy' status merely because the triggering/execution path succeeded.
trigger: Applies to any Clank whose health, alerting, or monitoring surface depends on distinguishing execution liveness from output/yield. A Clank with no scheduler and no external sources (e.g. a pure analysis tool over already-imported data) has neither axis and is out of scope by trigger. Does not require exactly two fields, one naming convention, or one score formula — any representation under which both dimensions remain independently determinable conforms.
rationale: The most convergently-independently-adopted pattern found across the fleet survey: seven of nine surveyed Clanks independently built some version of this two-axis split, several citing clank-architecture Fleet Law 3 ('scheduler invocation is not job success') by name in their own source comments. The sharpest incident evidence: a collector's ZERO_ITEMS run status was counted as a healthy success, masking 20 consecutive empty runs before the conflation was found and fixed; diagnostic-clank's own health contract was built directly from a comparable incident (a fleet reporting green while a delivery path was silently missing). chinese-tech-wire and korean-tech-wire independently converged on a near-identical found-versus-new zero-streak distinction with zero shared code, and korean-tech-wire's version correctly caught a real 8.5-day zero-new-observations block from a source-side network-level access restriction. Fleet Law 3 is ACTIVE, CI-enforced governance that already owns the underlying principle; this standard does not restate it, but ratifies the narrower slice Law 3 leaves open — a shared axis vocabulary and an explicit conflation-forbidden rule, across a fleet that currently uses nine different names for essentially the same two axes. A known, currently-unfixed exception exists (a health-score computation that starts at a fixed baseline and does not check enablement, validation status, or output realism) — cited as evidence of the gap this standard addresses, not as a finding against any specific Clank, which would require a separate conformance audit.
forbidden: Presenting a successful scheduler/trigger invocation, or a process exit code alone, as proof of output/yield health
Collapsing 'ran and produced nothing' into the same status as 'ran and succeeded' with no distinguishing signal available to a downstream reader
A health or alerting surface that cannot represent 'execution is live but output/yield is degraded or absent' as a distinct state from ordinary healthy operation
Treating the absence of new observations as automatically anomalous (or automatically healthy) without reference to that source's own expected behavior
acceptance: A downstream reader (operator surface, alerting rule, or another system) can determine execution/liveness health and output/yield health as independently queryable facts, whatever the underlying storage or naming convention
A run that executes successfully but yields zero or degraded output is distinguishable, in the Clank's own data, from a run that both executed and yielded successfully

Where a source has an established output baseline, an unexpected drop to zero is classifiable as a health concern distinct from ordinary healthy operation; where zero output is within that source's own expected behavior, it remains classifiable as healthy rather than forced into an anomalous state
No single boolean or status field is required to carry both dimensions' meaning at once — multiple independently-tracked dimensions conform equally to a two-field model

evidence.summary: A collector's ZERO_ITEMS run status was counted as HEALTHY by the health module, masking 20 consecutive zero-item runs until an explicit warning-streak setting was added.

Independently convergent found-vs-new zero-streak distinction with zero shared code; korean-tech-wire's version correctly caught an 8.5-day zero-new-observations block from a source-side access restriction.

Fleet Law 3 ('health honesty': scheduler invocation is not job success) is ACTIVE, CI-enforced governance naming this exact concern, with named historical violators across four Clanks; ADR-0007's HealthPayload contract was built directly from a green-dashboard/missing-delivery-path incident.

A documented, at-drafting-time-unfixed health-score computation starts at a fixed baseline and does not check enablement, validation status, or output realism — a single successful run with zero or garbage output scores fully healthy.

Independent implementations of the same axis split: delivery health kept structurally independent of source/collection health; catalog-shrink health classification kept independent of scheduler/process success.

notes: Pass 1 draft (docs/operations/pass1/dossier-ops-b-health-honesty-two-axis.md), from Pass 0B adjudication candidate OPS-B (docs/operations/pass0/candidates/ops-b-health-honesty-two-axis.md), merging Pass 0A clusters health-state-vs-scheduler-enabled-conflation and source-starvation-zero-vs-healthy-conflation (docs/operations/pass0/clusters/). Deliberately does not mandate exactly two fields, any particular axis name, or a score formula — any representation under which both dimensions remain independently determinable conforms. NARROW COMPLEMENT to clank-architecture Fleet Law 3 (ACTIVE): Law 3 owns the underlying health-honesty principle and is not restated; this standard ratifies only the axis-vocabulary/conflation-forbidden slice Law 3 leaves open. Distinct from STD-UI-COM-008/012, which govern operator-facing display of health/coverage semantics; this standard binds the underlying data/operations-layer state model those UI standards' displays must not misrepresent, not the display itself. Standards Clank defines the semantic invariant; clank-architecture's Fleet Laws and ADRs remain separate authority unless a later governance decision migrates or supersedes them — this standard does not claim to replace clank-architecture, and clank-architecture itself was not modified by this drafting pass. smartphone-clank's health_score() gap is cited as corpus evidence for the standard's existence, not as a conformance finding against that Clank, which would require a separate audit. PROPOSED — awaiting Pass 2 adversarial review and eventual operator ratification; not yet ratified, not self-ratified.
